subject.title: Dashboard: control hub — per-agent nesting, shared/private tabs, presence

question: Should OpenClaw accept this enabled-by-default dashboard control hub with device-id-scoped private tabs, presence, an unauthenticated static widget route, and new dependency graph surface after the code blockers are fixed?
rationale: The remaining issues are not only mechanical patch defects; they define a persistent storage contract, a privacy/security identity model, and dependency authorization that automation cannot choose for maintainers.

options.title: Require fixes and owner review
options.body: Keep the PR open, require the storage/CSP/entrypoint/labeler/artifact/proof fixes on a clean stack, then have a maintainer/security owner accept the privacy and dependency boundary.

options.title: Accept the boundary after fixes
options.body: A maintainer/security owner may approve device-id private tabs and the dependency graph once the concrete patch blockers and real proof are resolved.

options.title: Pause or close the bundled direction
options.body: If maintainers do not want this default bundled dashboard surface, route the idea back to plugin or ClawHub design and close the stacked PRs deliberately.

recommendation.title: Require fixes and owner review
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, require the storage/CSP/entrypoint/labeler/artifact/proof fixes on a clean stack, then have a maintainer/security owner accept the privacy and dependency boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent UI/plugin-state work and the product/security nature of the dashboard boundary make this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
